rationale:
Evidence: the best design so far is iteration 6 (909.8): kp 2.25, kd 1.2, ki 0, base 1.2, 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.03 m, mass 0.6 kg, body 0.14 m, wheel track 0.14 m. Its oval (20/20 finishes, 2.05 s) and s-bend (20/20, 2.38 s) are solid. The slalom is the gap: 16/20 finishes, 4 off-track exits, 0.2 line-loss events per run, and rms 0.012 m. Iteration 7 showed that lowering kp to 2.0 hurt (856.1): slalom finishes fell to 11/20, and line-loss events rose to 0.6. So the slalom failures are not overshoot that a lower kp can fix. Less turn authority causes the robot to undershoot and lose the line. Iteration 6 also showed that raising kd from 0.9 to 1.2 helped, and steering oscillation is still low (about 0.26), so the loop is not jittering.

Change: a single-variable change from iteration 6, raising kd from 1.2 to 1.5 with kp held at 2.25. More derivative action should damp the entry into tight slalom bends, where the signal changes fastest, without changing the steady-state response. Iteration 6 is the reference, and the trend from kd 0.9 to 1.2 was positive. Geometry and base speed stay fixed to isolate the effect.

Expected result: slalom finishes rise to 0.85 or higher and the slalom mean to about 850 or more, with oval and s-bend near iteration 6 values. Steering oscillation should stay below 0.35. Hypotheses: (H1) the slalom off-track exits come from fast entry transients, so more kd reduces them; (H2) if oscillation rises above 0.35 or control_effort jumps, kd has reached its useful limit and the next step is ki 0.1 with kd 1.2; (H3) if line_loss_events stay near 0.2 on the slalom, the loss comes from the sensor footprint and the next change should be to 12 mm sensors or a wider spread. Measurements wanted per track: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness, to separate line loss from transient overshoot.
